text:
Tessaly Fjord’s tidal plant is rated at 240 megawatts, according to project operator Bracken Vale Energy, which confirmed the figure in a filing Tuesday. The facility, now entering final commissioning, sits on the inner edge of the fjord and uses 32 submerged turbines to capture peak tidal flows. Bracken Vale said first commercial power is due in November, with annual output estimated at 930 gigawatt-hours.

Construction costs were put at 1.8 billion crowns, about 6% above budget after winter delays and cabling work. For the tidal-power sector, the rating is a useful benchmark: one of the largest grid-connected marine projects to date, and a sign lenders are warming to predictable, baseload-style renewables.
